# esa mark — geometry handoff

Drop-in geometry for the `esa` loading mark. **Do not hand-tune these numbers.** They were
derived from `fonts/Sato-Regular.woff` itself, which is why the light lands on the letters.

## How it was derived (reproducible)

1. `Sato-Regular.woff` -> TTF (fontTools), glyphs `e s a` set at their natural advances
   (1134 / 959 / 1135), baseline at y=0, units-per-em 2000.
2. Rasterised at 1000 px/em and thinned (Zhang-Suen) to the **stroke centrelines**.
3. The skeleton graph came out with 5 terminals and 3 junctions. Its branches are the
   real strokes of the letters.
4. One closed route was stitched through those branches, following Ethan's arrow sketch:

   | order | stroke |
   |-------|--------|
   | 1 | **e**: crossbar rightward, up the right, over the top leftward, back to the left junction |
   | 2 | **e**: down the left, around the bottom, out at the lower-right terminal |
   | 3 | connector -> **s** |
   | 4 | **s**: up the left of the bowl, over the top, out at the top-right terminal |
   | 5 | connector -> **a** |
   | 6 | **a**: bowl top leftward, down the left, along the bottom rightward |
   | 7 | **a**: up the stem |
   | 8 | **a**: up the right shoulder, over the top leftward, out at the top-left terminal |
   | 9 | connector -> **s** |
   | 10 | **s**: down the right, along the bottom leftward, out at the bottom-left terminal |
   | 11 | connector -> **e** (closes the loop) |

   Every connector is a cubic with control points on the incoming/outgoing tangents, so the
   whole loop is G1-continuous: **no cusps, no reversals, no sharp turn-arounds.**

## Numbers

- viewBox: `15 -1146 3241 1234`
- closed path length: 12,899 glyph units
- the letters path and the motion path are in the **same** coordinate system, so alignment is
  exact at any rendered size. Never scale one without the other.

## Motion path (closed loop) — FINAL, drawn by Ethan

49 anchors, closed double figure-eight, 12,899 glyph units long.
Median distance from the Sato stroke centrelines: **4 units** (the stroke half-width is ~50),
so the light rides the letterforms. The two big crossings sit in the gaps at
(1098, -365) and (2091, -616) — between **e** and **s**, and between **s** and **a**.

```js
// One light. Constant speed. Infinite. Never reverses.
(function(){
  var root    = document.querySelector('.esa-mark');
  var measure = root.querySelector('.esa-measure');
  var head    = root.querySelector('.esa-head');
  var glow    = root.querySelector('.esa-glow');
  var trails  = [].slice.call(root.querySelectorAll('.esa-trail'));  // t3, t2, t1 in DOM order
  var mult    = [2.1, 1.0, 0.32];          // trail length multipliers, same DOM order
  var total   = measure.getTotalLength();

  var PERIOD = 16;      // seconds for one full loop — Ethan wants it slow
  var TRAIL  = 0.11;    // base trail length as a fraction of the loop
  var t = 0, last = 0, running = true;

  if (window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) running = false;

  // Settle when the visitor first interacts with the page.
  ['pointerdown','keydown','wheel'].forEach(function(ev){
    window.addEventListener(ev, function(){ running = false; }, {once:true, passive:true});
  });

  function place(){
    var len = t * total;
    for (var i = 0; i < trails.length; i++){
      var seg = Math.max(24, TRAIL * total * mult[i]);
      trails[i].setAttribute('stroke-dasharray',  seg + ' ' + (total - seg));
      trails[i].setAttribute('stroke-dashoffset', (seg - len).toFixed(2));
    }
    var p = measure.getPointAtLength(len);
    head.setAttribute('cx', p.x); head.setAttribute('cy', p.y);
    glow.setAttribute('cx', p.x); glow.setAttribute('cy', p.y);
  }

  function frame(now){
    if (!last) last = now;
    var dt = Math.min(0.1, (now - last) / 1000); last = now;
    if (running) t = (t + dt / PERIOD) % 1;
    place();
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }
  place(); requestAnimationFrame(frame);
})();
```

```css
.esa-mark svg      { display:block; width:100%; height:auto; }
.esa-glyphs        { fill:#2b2b2b; }          /* on an ink ground */
/* paper ground instead: .esa-glyphs{fill:#d7d4cc} and swap the light to #7a3f06 / #d98a2b */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ .esa-trail, .esa-glow { opacity:0 } }
```

## Gotchas

- The trail is a **dash on the closed path**, not a sprite. That is what keeps it glued to the
  letterforms; a `<circle>` following `offset-path` drifts when the path is re-scaled.
- `stroke-dashoffset = trailLength - travelled`. Getting the sign wrong puts the trail *ahead*
  of the light.
- Do not re-type the `d` strings. Copy them.
- The `s` diagonal is deliberately not traced — the outbound and return strands pass either
  side of it. That is what Ethan's sketch shows.
